body: I was originally struggling to symbolicate our 2nd most prevalent crash,. but have now managed. Its actually the same as Crash 1 and Crash 1b (for some reason, Google play grouped those 2 again as a separate crash, so I'll just add the data points I captured here and to [@](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112158)

In addition to #114073, I have created https://github.com/clayjohn/godot/tree/RD-free-rid-list which should give us a bit more info. 

One theory is that some other thread is somehow freeing an RID in the middle of the creation of the draw list. It seems impossible since everything should be happening on the render thread. But it would be good to know if somehow some process on the render thread is freeing the uniform set RID between being bound to the draw list and when drawing actually happens

This branch alone isn't very helpful. But if anyone is ever able to reproduce this issue locally, it can be used to help narrow down the problem further.

Thanks to @AdriaandeJongh's investigation we have a pretty good idea about what is causing this. 

`RenderingDeviceDriverVulkan::uniform_set_create()` is failing due to the fragmentation in the related descriptor set pool. 

This causes the uniform set in `MaterialStorage::MaterialData::update_parameters_uniform_set()` to get set to `RID()`. Which in turn leads the 2D renderer to not bind a uniform set. 

In DEBUG builds this isn't an issue since we have a debug check to ensure that all uniform sets are bound:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8a6408c1ceaac721f7594a864fa98234644a19d5/servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp#L4999

In release builds we just crash instead further below since we assume the uniform set exists (this is no longer true since the inclusion of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/114073). 

There are 4 options to fix this at different layers:
1. We can simply abort a batch early if it needs a material uniform set but none is provided. Currently the code is happy to render a batch without a material uniform set since many shaders don't need one. 
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8a6408c1ceaac721f7594a864fa98234644a19d5/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/renderer_canvas_render_rd.cpp#L2325-L2329
This is a bad solution though since it will create a lot of runtime checks that shouldn't be needed
2. We can move the check above out of the DEBUG check so it is included in release builds. Again, this would avoid the crash, but its not ideal as it adds a run time cost that should not be necessary.
3. We can try to reduce how often material uniform sets are freed and updated. Possibly even adding in a path to use `vkUpdateDescriptorSets` to avoid having to free and update them at all. This would be a useful performance improvement overall, but it may not fix the bug entirely. It would definitely make it more rare though. This deserves some investigation, because it is possible that there is a bug that is making us update uniform sets too frequently.
4. We can fix the bug that is making `RenderingDeviceDriverVulkan::uniform_set_create()` fail. This is the correct fix and should be sufficient alone to fix this bug. 

### Fixing `RenderingDeviceDriverVulkan::uniform_set_create()`

In discussion with @blueskythlikesclouds and Adriaan, we have learned the following:
1. `vkAllocateDescriptorSets()` is failing with `VK_ERROR_FRAGMENTED_POOL`. Due to how the drivers work, this is a very rare error on most GPUs. But it is easy to trigger on Mali. 
2. We manually manage descriptor set pools and keep track of when they are full. Clearly our code for tracking their fullness doesn't take fragmentation into account. 
3. We dynamically create more pools as needed, so we can create more pools, but we need to do that _after_ finding out a pool is fragmented. 
4. The size of each pool is controlled by `rendering/rendering_device/vulkan/max_descriptors_per_pool` and is set to a very low value by default. This value can be raised by users as a potential workaround to this issue

It sounds like the solution is going to involve falling back and creating a new pool when an allocation fails. This will require reorganizing our current system a little bit to take that into account. 

At the same time, we need to investigate further to understand why we are getting `VK_ERROR_FRAGMENTED_POOL` and not `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_POOL_MEMORY` since it sounds like Mali devices may not return memory to the pool when descriptor sets are freed ([source](https://documentation-service.arm.com/static/67a62b17091bfc3e0a947695?token=)):

> Arm GPUs ignore the VK_DESCRIPTOR_POOL_CREATE_FREE_DESCRIPTOR_SET_BIT flag, but applications must still support the specification. This means that if VK_DESCRIPTOR_POOL_CREATE_FREE_DESCRIPTOR_SET_BIT is set, then you must still check for pool fragmentation. If the flag is not set, then you must not free individual descriptor sets, and only use vkAllocateDescriptorSets() and vkResetDescriptorPool().

My gut feeling is that:
1. Mali never returns memory to the memory pool when we call `vkFreeDescriptorSets`
2. We are calculating the memory pool size slightly wrong
3. Therefore, the pool doesn't actually fill up (there is some wasted space at the end), but there isn't enough space to allocate another set so we get `VK_ERROR_FRAGMENTED_POOL`
4. Since we rely on manually tracking allocations, we never allocate another pool since we think there should be enough space left. 

If my theory is correct, then in addition to adding a new pool when we get `VK_ERROR_FRAGMENTED_POOL`, we need to validate that our current approach is correctly sizing the pool in the first place and our tracking information can correctly identify when a new pool is needed
